public_rationale: Supported on the ordinary reading of “that doesn’t mean”: similar false statements alone do not establish shared mechanisms. Human experimental evidence separates deceptive intention from statement truth, while GPT documentation identifies a model training process without establishing its equivalence to human deception. This is an inference from the cited evidence, not a direct comparison with Santos. Research also reports shared language-processing principles between brains and models, so the evidence would not support a broader assertion that they have nothing in common.
limitations: Support applies to the caution about inference, not to a claim that all underlying mechanisms differ.
The human experiment studied laboratory participants, not Santos.
The quoted evidence is from abstracts; it does not provide a complete mechanistic account.
This assessment does not establish that GPT lacks intent.
